raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`/generative_scoring` now accepts `cache_salt` and applies it to every item's prompt, allowing prefix-cache reuse to be scoped by salt in multi-tenant deployments.

## Claims

- Validates `cache_salt` with the shared validator and passes it to every item's engine input.
- Preserves the existing behavior when `cache_salt` is omitted or `null`.

## Validation

- Generative-scoring tests and shared request-validation tests passed.
- Ran `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` locally and sent HTTP requests to `/generative_scoring`. Verified cache reuse with the same salt, no reuse between different salts, and the same scores across these requests.

## Details

The request model did not expose `cache_salt`, and prompts were built without it. This change reuses the shared validator and the existing `tokens_input` support.

---

- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.

</details>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

LGTM — small, well-contained change that follows the existing cache_salt pattern used by other endpoints.

What was reviewed: the new `cache_salt` field and its `model_validator(mode="before")` guard (reuses the shared `validate_cache_salt` helper, matches the non-dict-body guard pattern already tested for other request models); the threading of `request.cache_salt` into `tokens_input(...)` for every item in `_build_prompts`; and the doc updates cross-linking `/generative_scoring` into the security guide. Tests cover both text and pre-tokenized inputs, salted and unsalted requests, and non-object body validation.


<details>
<summary>Extended reasoning...</summary>

Diff touches vllm/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/serving.py (new optional cache_salt field, before-validator, and pass-through to tokens_input) plus docs and tests; it reuses an already-reviewed shared validator rather than introducing new security logic, and the pattern mirrors cache_salt handling already present in other endpoints (chat/completions/pooling/structured-decisions), with test coverage added for both the salted/unsalted cases and the non-object body guard.

</details>
